title: Bell + inertia + zeta: three measured scientific outcomes
description: Synthetic and classical: three measured outcomes from three sources. Bell (1964): a local hidden-variable model (Monte Carlo) stays at CHSH |S| <= 2 while the quantum singlet reaches 2 sqrt(2), and at equal settings the outcomes are perfectly anticorrelated. Moment of inertia: the disk-slice integral of a solid sphere gives (2/5) M R^2, and the sphere carries 3/5 of a thin shell's inertia. Riemann (1859): the first ten zeta zeros on the critical line, computed from scratch by Euler-Maclaurin summation, land on the established values, and ten zeros sit below t = 50 as Riemann-von Mangoldt predicts. Measured claims with frozen bars.
